$comment: Mission 1.42. The authored documentary input to the convergent-scope reliability packet, keyed by nothing and read by build_convergent_reliability_packet.py. It contains FACTS, QUESTIONS and APPLICABILITY JUDGEMENTS about documents. It contains no reliability value, no range and no threshold adjective for the scope under review, and a test scans for all three. A $comment is where a rule is written and a rule may name what it forbids; a field may not.

what_reliability_means.the_question: How dependable is THIS kind of measurement for THIS kind of proposition?
it_is_not: whether TED is legally approved for use
whether public procurement is a reliable domain
whether CPV division 92 is commercially attractive
whether EUR is a reliable currency
whether recreational, cultural and sporting services are worth pursuing
what_reliability_means.scope_is_five_fields: source_id, resource_id, record_kind_id, claim_type, proposition_kind. Matched in full or not at all. No CPV division, no currency, no notice class, no subject and no row id enters it -- ADR-026 and the live model both, verified against the contract rather than assumed.

detailed_versus_convergent.detailed_asserts: that within a NAMED bounded set of notices, the largest stated amount of a named semantic exceeded the smallest, or equalled it. The cohort membership is part of the identity.
detailed_versus_convergent.convergent_asserts: that the source published AT LEAST ONE bounded set of notices of a named class under a named classification division whose stated amounts of that semantic stand in the named relation. Cohort membership moved to Evidence provenance and is no longer part of the identity.
shared_measurement_semantics: the same source, the same resource and the same record kind
the same amount semantic: BT-161, the value of all contracts awarded in a notice, including options and renewals
the same field: notice level, non-repeatable, with a companion currency field
the same reading direction: SROS reports what TED STATED, and never what anyone paid
the same conformance boundary: TED validates that a value is present and well formed, never that it is correct
reliability_questions_that_are_shared: does the stated amount mean what the SDK says it means
can a stated amount be wrong without TED detecting it
can a notice be corrected or amended after publication
is the classification assigned by the contracting authority to its own contract
reliability_questions_that_are_NEW: an EXISTENTIAL proposition is monotone: once a qualifying cohort has been published, no later notice can make it false. A reviewer must decide whether that makes the proposition more dependable, or merely harder to falsify -- these are not the same thing.
the proposition carries NO PERIOD, because H-37 leaves TED's publication-date semantics unestablished. So it asserts something about the source's publication with no time bound at all.

the assertion is about a CLASS rather than about named notices, so it depends on the classification being what the source says it is for at least the witnessing cohort -- and on SROS having projected that classification correctly.

two cohorts are asserted to witness ONE proposition. That is an SROS convergence step, and if its identity fields were wrong, a Claim would carry Evidence that does not bear on it. This failure mode does not exist for the detailed proposition.
detailed_versus_convergent.what_did_not_change: the underlying TED values, fields and semantics. Mission 1.39 changed the shape of the proposition, not the measurement.

documentary_review_matrix.question: What does the measured amount mean?
documentary_review_matrix.factual_answer: BT-161 is 'The value of all contracts awarded in this notice, including options and renewals'.
documentary_review_matrix.relevance: It bounds what the amounts in either proposition are. An amount including options and renewals is not a price and not a payment, and both propositions inherit that.

documentary_review_matrix.question: How is the amount represented, and is a currency paired with it?
documentary_review_matrix.factual_answer: TOTAL_VALUE is BT-161, notice level, non-repeatable, at efac:NoticeResult/cbc:TotalAmount, with a companion currency field.
documentary_review_matrix.relevance: The companion currency field is what makes a currency-pure cohort expressible at all. It is a fact about the FIELD, and it does not say the value in it is right.

documentary_review_matrix.question: Does TED validate that a stated amount is correct?
documentary_review_matrix.factual_answer: 60 published rules govern where BT-161 may appear. All are presence, absence or notice-type constraints; none concerns the amount's correctness.
documentary_review_matrix.relevance: The central shared limitation. Conformance validation is not truth validation, and a value can be wrong and still conform.

documentary_review_matrix.question: Can a result value be withheld from publication?
documentary_review_matrix.document: eForms SDK 1.15.1 business-term definitions, BT-195 to BT-198
documentary_review_matrix.factual_answer: Result values, of which BT-161 is one, may be withheld from immediate publication with a justification and a later date.
documentary_review_matrix.relevance: Its WEIGHT differs between the two propositions, and that difference is a reviewer's to judge. A detailed cohort covers only the published subset, so withholding bounds what the cohort represents. An EXISTENTIAL proposition asserts that something WAS published, so an unpublished value does not falsify it -- which does not make the measurement better, only the proposition narrower.

documentary_review_matrix.question: Can a notice be corrected or amended after publication, and can that change whether a cohort still qualifies?
documentary_review_matrix.relevance: OPEN. No retrieved first-party document establishes TED's correction and amendment policy for a published BT-161, nor whether a corrected notice supersedes an earlier one in this resource. This is the question a reviewer is most likely to want answered, and no document currently held answers it.

documentary_review_matrix.question: Who assigns the CPV classification, and can it change after publication?
documentary_review_matrix.factual_answer: A contracting authority assigns a CPV code to ITS OWN contract. A CPV class therefore contains procurements and never products. Whether an assigned code can later be corrected is NOT established by any document held.
documentary_review_matrix.relevance: The convergent proposition asserts about a division, so what the division membership rests on is load-bearing. Half of this is established and half is open, and the open half is recorded rather than smoothed over.

documentary_review_matrix.question: Does the source report the values, or does SROS infer them?
documentary_review_matrix.document: eForms SDK 1.15.1 field repository plus the collector and normalizer contracts
documentary_review_matrix.factual_answer: The values are read from the notice payload as published. No amount is computed, no currency is converted, and no value is imputed.
documentary_review_matrix.relevance: It fixes what a reliability judgement is ABOUT: the dependability of a source-reported figure, not of an SROS estimate.

failure_modes.failure_mode: a stated amount is wrong and conforms anyway
failure_modes.effect_on_the_bounded_proposition: the relation between two stated amounts could differ from the relation between the underlying facts. The proposition says the STATED amounts differ, so it survives, but a reader who takes it for a fact about contracts does not.
failure_modes.current_mitigation: the claim's own wording is bounded to what the source stated
failure_modes.residual_unknown: the rate at which stated amounts are wrong is unmeasured and unmeasurable from the source's own documents

failure_modes.failure_mode: a result value is withheld from publication
failure_modes.effect_on_the_bounded_proposition: the published subset is not the whole. For an existential this does not falsify the claim; it bounds what the claim covers.
failure_modes.current_mitigation: the proposition is existential and says 'at least one bounded set'
failure_modes.residual_unknown: how often withholding happens in this classification

failure_modes.failure_mode: a published notice is later corrected, amended or superseded
failure_modes.effect_on_the_bounded_proposition: a witnessing cohort could stop exhibiting the asserted relation, or its classification could change. The Claim would then rest on Evidence whose witness no longer qualifies.
failure_modes.current_mitigation: none. The corpus was collected once and nothing re-checks it.
failure_modes.residual_unknown: OPEN, and it is the largest one. No held document establishes the correction policy.

failure_modes.failure_mode: two currencies compared as one distribution
failure_modes.effect_on_the_bounded_proposition: would make the asserted relation meaningless
failure_modes.current_mitigation: currency is a cohort-key field since procurement-value-contrast 1.1.0, and a mixed cohort is refused with INCOMPATIBLE_SERIES. Both guards are present: the key prevents the mixture and the validation catches a caller who forces one.
failure_modes.residual_unknown: none identified for currency; the guard is structural and tested

failure_modes.failure_mode: a per-lot value compared with a whole-notice value
failure_modes.current_mitigation: amount scope is a cohort-key field since 1.1.0, with the same double guard

failure_modes.failure_mode: a notice's classification is projected to the wrong division
failure_modes.effect_on_the_bounded_proposition: the Claim would assert about a class the witness is not in
failure_modes.current_mitigation: a notice classified across several divisions joins NO cohort rather than the first one listed; the division is read from the notice's own codes
failure_modes.residual_unknown: whether a single-division notice's code is itself correct is a SOURCE question, not a projection one

failure_modes.failure_mode: two cohorts that do not witness the same proposition are treated as if they did
failure_modes.effect_on_the_bounded_proposition: the Claim would carry Evidence that does not bear on it. THIS FAILURE MODE DOES NOT EXIST FOR THE DETAILED PROPOSITION, and it is the one convergence introduced.
failure_modes.current_mitigation: source-published-value-contrast-witnessed@1.0.0 fixes ten identity fields, refuses a fact set carrying anything it does not classify, and is deterministic over persisted facts with no similarity, no embedding and no model
failure_modes.residual_unknown: whether the ten identity fields are the RIGHT ten is a design judgement that real data has now exercised twice and not refuted

failure_modes.effect_on_the_bounded_proposition: would manufacture corroboration out of one observation
failure_modes.current_mitigation: witness_key over the witness facts, plus Evidence identity repaired in Mission 1.41 so an interpreter version bump can no longer insert a second row
failure_modes.residual_unknown: none identified; both guards are tested

failure_modes.failure_mode: the acquisition window shaped which cohorts exist
failure_modes.effect_on_the_bounded_proposition: the witnesses that exist are the ones two frozen seven-day windows contained. An existential is not damaged by this -- it needs one qualifying cohort, not a representative sample -- but the proposition must never be read as saying anything about how COMMON such cohorts are.
failure_modes.current_mitigation: the proposition's own wording is existential and its does_not_establish list names prevalence, proportion and typicality
failure_modes.residual_unknown: none for the existential reading; the risk is entirely in how a later reader summarises it

engineering_validation_inputs.$note: §9. Recorded SEPARATELY from documentary basis, and deliberately NOT offered as one. These are facts about software behaving as specified. The reliability contract admits documents and a reviewer's documented judgement as basis; a passing test is neither, and rewarding the system numerically because its tests pass is the failure §7 names.
inputs: Mission 1.41 re-derived the historical division-90 Signal under extractor 1.1.0 from its exact persisted inputs and reproduced magnitude, currency, direction, amount types, amount scopes and classification codes identically, with its three inputs still forming one group.
Mission 1.39 proved the convergence contract on synthetic fixtures through the real repository: one Claim, two Evidence rows, one revision, idempotent replay.
Mission 1.41 repaired Evidence identity so that re-interpreting an unchanged Signal under a new interpreter version cannot insert a second row.
The currency and amount-scope cohort guards are exercised by tests, including a forced mixed cohort that still refuses.
engineering_validation_inputs.what_they_establish: that the implementation does what its specification says.
engineering_validation_inputs.what_they_do_not_establish: anything about how dependable TED's source-reported amounts are.

existing_basis_applicability.why: It defines what the measured amount MEANS, and the convergent proposition asserts about the same amounts. Nothing about the definition depends on whether the cohort is named.
The field, its level and its companion currency are the same. If anything it is more load-bearing now: the companion currency field is what makes a currency-pure cohort expressible.
TED validates conformance and never correctness. That limitation is identical under either proposition.

existing_basis_applicability.document_title: eForms SDK 1.15.1 business-term definitions, BT-195 to BT-198
existing_basis_applicability.why: The FACT is unchanged and its WEIGHT is not. Under the detailed proposition, withholding bounds what a named cohort represents. Under an existential it cannot falsify the claim, because the claim asserts that something WAS published. The reviewer decides how much that matters; software should not decide it for them.

open_questions: Whether TED permits a published BT-161 to be corrected or amended, and whether a corrected notice supersedes an earlier one in this resource. NO first-party document currently held answers this, and it is the question with the most direct bearing on whether a witnessing cohort still witnesses.
Whether an assigned CPV code can be corrected after publication. Mission 1.35 established WHO assigns a code; nothing held establishes whether it can change.

Whether an existential proposition with no period is more dependable than a bounded one, or merely harder to falsify. This is a judgement about the proposition rather than a fact about the source, and it is exactly the kind of thing a named reviewer is for.
How often division-92 notices withhold their result values. Unmeasured, and not measurable from the source's own documentation.
what_a_value_would_not_do: it would not calibrate anything: REFERENCE_PROFILE_V1 stays UNCALIBRATED, and reliability review is not calibration
it would not establish independence: both Claims' Evidence stays UNKNOWN with zero groups, and DISJOINT observation membership is a different axis
it would not become a TED-wide coefficient: the existing detailed scope keeps its own assessment and neither reaches the other
it would not apply to CPV division 92 as a category: the scope carries no classification division at all
it would not make the Claims true, and it would not make the aggregation output a probability
it would not change any source's governance standing
what_this_packet_is_not: it is not a recommendation, and it contains no value, no range and no threshold adjective for the scope under review
it is not an assessment: nothing is persisted and ReliabilityAssessments stay at two
it does not name a reviewer: §17 forbids inferring one from a git author, a PR author, an OS username, an earlier assessment or this conversation
it does not treat the existing TED 0.5 as a baseline, a starting point or a default; that value belongs to a different proposition kind and appears here only as historical other-scope context
